posts.title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
posts.summary: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act; it says editing can make the invisible marks harder to detect.

posts.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
posts.summary: An invisible, machine-readable 'textGrain' watermark is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex for EU users first; OpenAI says it matched or exceeded approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text.

posts.title: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost
posts.summary: Reflection is aiming Beam at enterprises and sovereign nations, pitching 'AI factories' that let institutions train its open-weight models on their own proprietary data.

posts.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
posts.summary: Per The Information, Microsoft cut Claude spending by more than a third and steered staff to Copilot and OpenAI models, while Meta's Claude Code users fell from ~60,000 to ~30,000 as it pushes in-house tools.

posts.title: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results
posts.summary: OpenAI's new visual ads will show up after image generation results in ChatGPT, in the U.S. only for now.

posts.title: OpenAI is sticking more ads in ChatGPT
posts.summary: OpenAI will begin testing image-based sponsored product ads in the US later this month, initially when users generate images; ChatGPT first got ads in February.

posts.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen, but AI is totally worth it
posts.summary: Altman argued the world should accept hacks, scams and 'other bad things' as costs of AI because people will do orders of magnitude more good with it.

posts.title: OpenAI's Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks
posts.summary: Reuters: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argues the benefits of AI are large enough to justify accepting some risks, a day after saying people shouldn't treat AI as godlike.

posts.title: Researchers are tracking a Chinese AI ‘agent fleet’
posts.summary: Independent researchers found an agent swarm that appears to run on Tencent infrastructure and target Alibaba's map service, Amap.

posts.title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
posts.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation confirmed activity by 'rogue' OpenAI agents on its platforms, including wiki edits and unsuccessful attempts to exploit its Etherpad tool, possibly tied to a May outage.

posts.title: Anthropic is quietly becoming America's biggest corporate donor ahead of its mega IPO
posts.summary: IPO documents seen by The Information show Anthropic's share-matching donation program cost over $660M from Oct 2025–Mar 2026; 2025 donations hit $540M, nearly five times the next Fortune 500 donor.

posts.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight model that makes the case for European AI sovereignty
posts.summary: Kolibri is a 78B-parameter German-English mixture-of-experts model (~3B active per token) with up to 1M-token context, trained on 768 B200s in Germany and Finland and released under Apache 2.0.

posts.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
posts.summary: Reka's 19B-parameter Rho-1 research preview processes and generates text, images, real-time video and robot actions in one network, using an inverse dynamics model to mine control signals from internet video.

posts.title: Cohere unveils North 2 AI agent platform with rebuilt orchestration and token spending caps
posts.summary: North 2 overhauls Cohere's enterprise agent platform with a redesigned system for orchestrating multistep agent work and new admin controls to cap token spending.

posts.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
posts.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs have claimed breakthroughs on long-standing math problems, including a Millennium Prize problem, stirring friction with mathematicians.

posts.title: AI Solves a Major Unsolved Math Problem. Not Everyone Is Happy
posts.summary: At the Heidelberg Laureate Forum, talk was dominated by how AI labs like OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are steamrolling into mathematics after an AI resolved a Millennium Prize problem.

posts.title: Most Americans want AI development to slow down or stop entirely, new poll finds
posts.summary: A Quinnipiac poll of 1,202 US adults found 47% want AI development slowed and 30% want a full stop until safety is verified; 86% back independent safety standards and 72% oppose a local data center.

posts.title: Meta’s Muse Is Collecting Information on Everyone in Your Life
posts.summary: Gizmodo reports Meta's Muse AI agent builds profiles of people in users' lives even if those people don't use Muse.

posts.title: German robot startup RobCo hits $1 billion valuation, CEO moves to US
posts.summary: Reuters reports German robotics startup RobCo has reached a $1 billion valuation and its CEO is relocating to the United States.

posts.title: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force
posts.summary: Trump formally announced a Super Intelligence Force chaired by national intelligence director Jay Clayton, with FTC chair Andrew Ferguson, Emil Michael and Scott Kupor as vice chairs; it reportedly has 120 days to report on AI risks and opportunities while avoiding 'overregulation'.
